hook.text: The title's first half is a metaphor for dodging hard topics, and the second urges leaving the past behind.

sentences.text: Denzel Curry first pictured the album's themes in 2018, and began work on it after finishing Zuu, his 2019 album.
In a May 2020 interview he said he planned to retire from music after three more full-length projects.
He talked about retiring past alter egos such as Zeltron, Aquarius Killa and Raven Miyagi, in favor of his own personality and feelings.
The themes also drew on several works of cinema, among them the Dollars trilogy, Yojimbo, Seven Samurai and Ran.
Cardo, FnZ, Thundercat, JPEGMafia and Kenny Beats are among the producers.
Nathan Burgess mixed and engineered the record, and Chris Gehringer mastered it.
Robert Glasper plays keyboards, A-Trak handles the sampler on two tracks, and Bridget Perez adds background vocals.
Anna Wise, Thundercat, Sharina Castillo, Gaby Duran and Shawn K add extra vocals.
A remix of Walkin featuring Key Glock was the first single from the extended edition, in June 2022.
That edition followed in September 2022 with 10 new songs that Curry recorded with the Cold Blooded Soul Band.
It also brought two previously unreleased tracks, Larger Than Life and Chrome Hearts, the second featuring Zacari.
A livestream concert, Melt My Eyez: Live From the Komodo City Cafe, promoted it the day before.

listen_for.text: Robert Glasper is the featured guest on it.
It samples The Loving Touch, a song Keith Mansfield wrote and performed.
It samples Come Closer, a song performed by Salma Agha.
It samples Nothing Left to Do, performed by After All, and Karriem Riggins is a featured guest on it.
It samples Amen, Brother, a song the Winstons performed, and Slowthai is a featured guest on it.
